- Evidence set A (technical): architecture diagram showing where prompt/response logs reside, retention defaults, S3 buckets or DB names (redacted), and roles that can access logs.

Subject: Re: EuroBank: attestation request — AI prompt persistence & training exclusion

Hi Lars / Karine,

Quick technical clarifications:

- Hosted API behavior (default):
  * Inference path: requests are routed to the serving runtime. We maintain only an in-memory KV cache for live sessions to support streaming and short-context completion. That KV cache is ephemeral (purged within seconds/minutes after session end) unless the customer explicitly enables logging.
  * Request/response traces: by default, we do not persist full prompts/responses for Hosted API accounts. We do persist minimal telemetry (latency, error codes, token counts) for billing/observability.

- Optional persistence: customers can enable transcript retention for debugging/analytics; when enabled this stores artifacts in a customer-scoped storage location with configurable retention (30/90/365 days). Customers control access and retention via the Console and API.

- No-train guarantee: we offer a contractual "no-train" option. For Hosted, we enforce a logical flag on the account that prevents data from entering any model-training pipelines and marks collected transcripts as ineligible for internal training workflows. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customer data never leaves the customer's environment unless they choose to share it.

- Evidence artifacts we can provide this week: architecture diagram (VPC + storage flow), console screenshots showing retention toggles, an export of account-level flags (redacted), and a signed short-form attestation from Redwood Legal. KMS integration details available for Private customers only; Hosted supports customer-managed keys for log encryption at rest via a KMS integration.

I’ll attach an architecture PNG and a draft attestation text for Legal to review.

—Priyom
Priyom Das | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Lars / Karine,

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a short-form attestation for your procurement packet. Key points covered:

- Redwood will not use customer-provided data from the specified EuroBank account(s) to train, fine-tune, or improve any of Redwood’s or third-party models without explicit, documented consent.
- For Hosted accounts, retention of prompts/responses is disabled by default; any retention must be opt-in and is governed by the account’s admin controls.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer data remains in the customer-controlled environment and is not accessed for model training unless the customer opts in.
- We document technical controls and will provide architecture diagrams, console exports, and redacted logs as part of the evidence package.

Please review the attached attestation text and indicate any specific language EuroBank’s procurement/legal team would like adjusted. Once agreed, I can sign and return a PDF.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Grace / Camila / Priyom — thank you, that looks good and covers the core asks. A few small asks before procurement signs off:

1) Can you include a short sentence confirming the retention default window for optional transcript logging (we prefer 30 days unless explicitly extended).
2) Please add the specific SCC clause mapping (we will send a template SCC appendix; can you confirm acceptance of the latest SCCs EU Commission 2024 version).
3) For auditability, can you provide a single example export (redacted) showing the account-level no-train flag and a timestamped log entry proving the flag was set? Redaction of account identifiers is fine.

If you can provide those three items by end-of-day Friday (25 Jun), procurement will proceed to contract review. We appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Karine Dupont | Legal Counsel (Data Protection), EuroBank
